pull.title: rpc: parse each batch element into its own request
pull.body:
In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error reply with the id and version of the element before it.

`ExecuteHTTPRPC` parses every element of a batch into the same request object, and `parse()` throws on a non-object before it sets `id` and `m_json_version`. For `[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"getblockcount","id":"X"}, 2]` the reply has two objects with `"id":"X"`, one with a result and one with an error. If the first element is a notification, the error is dropped. I give each element its own copy of the request, which holds only the HTTP fields, so the error is the one the first element of a batch already gets. The new case in `interface_rpc.py` fails on master and passes with this change.

This is a reasonable follow up to #27101 and fixes something we missed from the jsonrpc 2.0 spec that could confuse consumers of the interface expecting unique IDs in batch responses.

Done: I removed the second `m_json_version` reset and simplified the test's asserts. The batch case now checks the valid reply, then that the error reply has another id and no `jsonrpc` field, which fails if the version reset stays where it was; the notification case checks that the error reply is there.

rpc: parse each batch element into its own request

In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error
reply with the id and version of the element before it. A client that
matches replies by id can take that error for the result of the
previous call. If the previous element was a 2.0 notification, the
error is dropped.

Every element was parsed into the same JSONRPCRequest. I give each
element its own copy of the request before parsing, which holds only
the HTTP fields at that point. The functional test covers the two
cases.

comments.body: Thanks, I'll take this if I need to push again.

While it does make for a more surgical fix, it doesn't feel robust to reset individual fields.

Would prefer something closer to https://github.com/hodlinator/bitcoin/tree/pr/36642_suggestions where in commit db01f652d2e092440a90f9339e86b804327b0faf a fresh `JSONRPCRequest` is created for each element in a batch. Maybe it could be simplified a bit (further), curious what others think.

Yes, a fresh request per element is sturdier, and I'm glad to take your commits, here or in a follow-up, whichever you and others prefer.

One condition: your first commit leaves three throws outside any try, so they lose their JSON-RPC error replies. A body of `2` now gets HTTP 500 with a plain `unknown error` instead of the -32700 "Top-level object parse error". I'd take the commits once the refactor keeps those three replies as they are.

@fametrano another reminder to write your comments yourself. Both comments left here so far were not nits, but requests to change your code in this pull request. If you find problems with them, just improve them, don't ask for exact copies from reviewers.
Pushed 5861dd29a7 with your suggestion: each batch element now gets its own request. `request.cpp` is back to master.
